acceptance: Each listed caller's current behaviour on a failed download is recorded first (retries or not, what the failure leads to), from reading the code on current develop.

pr-arm: a unit test with a stubbed runner feeds a 503 ServerBusy response then success and shows the verdict is evaluated; a test feeds persistent 503 and shows pr-arm refuses after the bounded budget with an outcome line naming the transient cause; a test shows a network timeout on the ruleset read is retried the same way.

If the gate decision chooses the check-run or status route, pr-arm reads the verdict there, the artifact read path is removed (no fallback), and a test shows a missing or mismatched-head verdict still refuses.

Every other caller that gates a decision either retries transient failures with bounded backoff (with a test) or the item records why not; nightly-v2.yml's best-effort read either stays with a recorded reason or fails visibly.
One real `make pr-arm WAIT=` run on a PR after the change arms normally; its outcome is quoted in the closeout.
context:
Decision gate: Before coding, choose between (a) bounded retry around the artifact download and (b) publishing the fast-duration verdict as a check-run output or commit status so arming no longer reads blob storage. Criteria: (b) wins if the verdict can be bound to the exact head SHA and produced by the same job; otherwise (a). Record the choice and reason on this item. This item needs pr-arm-cut-repeated-github-reads-20261117 (actively claimed, same file): wait for it to merge and use its read helper rather than adding a second one.

Item guardrails: An unreadable or failed read is never a pass; retries are bounded inside the existing WAIT budget and never extend it; no read result is cached across wait cycles; no change to required checks, rulesets or the review gate; retry only idempotent GETs.

Verification rubric: Pass = all acceptance tests green in make pr-preflight, plus the real pr-arm run quoted. Fail = any path where a persistent download failure arms the PR.

Base guardrails: work in a linked worktree (make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight), never the primary clone; one PR per repository; no live-cloud runs and no credentials in Git or logs; heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers, servers) only through lock-taking entry points or make heavy-run after make heavy-status; never start deliberate CPU, memory or disk load, and tests inject readings instead; comment policy (make comment-policy-check); changelog.d fragment for user-facing change. Re-verify every cited file and line on current develop before acting; they are hints and drift. Stop and report instead of widening scope; scope removed during review is re-homed to a named item or dropped by the owner with a reason.

Origin: Found 2026-11-17 by a read-only root-cause investigation of the egress 503.

Owner decision 2026-11-17: route (a): bounded retry on the artifact download, not a move to a check-run output. Deliver in one PR with pr-arm-github-rate-limit-backoff-20261112 (same read helper), after pr-arm-cut-repeated-github-reads-20261117 merges.
description:
Problem: on 2026-11-17 `make pr-arm` for PR #4274 refused with `HTTP 503: Egress is over the account limit` while downloading the 535-byte artifact fast-duration-verdict-4274-c6d657102. The 503 is Azure ServerBusy on GitHub's shared multi-tenant results storage (productionresultssa9), not a BenchBox quota; githubstatus showed no incident and a retry about 25 minutes later succeeded. In scripts/pr_arm.py (about line 277 on develop at 2026-11-17) `gh run download` runs once and any non-zero exit becomes a refusal. The same day a pr-arm for PR #4276 refused on `dial tcp ...: i/o timeout` reading the develop ruleset; an immediate retry armed. Other artifact readers that may have the same weakness, NOT yet verified per caller: scripts/release_artifact_consumer.py (artifact zip read ~854), scripts/release_reuse_uat_evidence.py (_gh_bytes ~369/386), scripts/sqlglot_delivery.py (~341), scripts/trunk_duration_trend.py (~365; has a sample-attempt loop at ~404 that may or may not retry a failed download), scripts/trunk_uat.py (~564), .github/workflows/fast-duration-baseline-refresh.yml (~101, 247, 251). .github/workflows/nightly-v2.yml (~494) downloads prior throughput baselines with `|| true` and prints the count found; that may be intended best-effort.

Outcome: transient GitHub failures (5xx, ServerBusy, network timeouts) on artifact reads that gate a decision are retried within a bounded budget and never treated as a pass; a persistent failure still refuses with a clear outcome line.
